name: particles-in-consensus
title: Particles in a consensus tissue: Smoldyn molecules bounded by a boundary three tissue simulators agree on
question: Can a Smoldyn particle sim be confined inside each cell of a tri-coupled consensus tissue, bounded by a boundary whose shape is vertex, position is the munk consensus and area is CPM?

study_card.goal: Confine spatially-resolved chemistry inside a multi-paradigm consensus tissue.
study_card.mechanism: On the tri-coupled consensus, each cell's vertex polygon (the consensus shape, placed at the munk-consensus position and sized by CPM area) is a reflective Smoldyn surface; an A+B<->C sim runs confined to it.
study_card.why_before_next: Shows the consensus boundary is a real, usable object: molecules reflect off a boundary three tissue simulators agree on, composing particle chemistry with a multi-paradigm tissue.
study_card.expected_result: Molecules stay confined inside a boundary three tissue simulators agree on, while the consensus holds -- spatially-resolved chemistry inside a multi-paradigm tissue.
study_card.main_expert_question: When the three backends briefly disagree (a transient spread spike), should particles follow the vertex shape, the CPM area, or a blended boundary?
